question.:question/problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}{y}^{2}\,dx-{x}^{2}\,dy,$ where $C$ is part of the circle ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=1$ traversed in the counterclockwise direction from the point $A(1,0)$ to the point $B(0,1).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since $C$ is a circle of radius $1$ centered at the origin, it can be parametrized as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =x(t)\,i+y(t)\,j=\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j,\,t\in [0,\frac{\pi }{2}]\end{aligned}
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j=-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}{y}^{2}\,dx-{x}^{2}\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{y}^{2}\,\frac{dx}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t-{x}^{2}\,\frac{dy}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}({y}^{2}\,\frac{dx}{\text{d}t}-{x}^{2}\,\frac{dy}{\text{d}t})\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)-(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}-{sin}^{3}⁡t-{cos}^{3}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & =-{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{sin}^{3}⁡t+{cos}^{3}⁡t\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Evaluate ${\int }_{C}\frac{y\,dy-x\,dx}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}},$ where $C$ is part of the circle ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=1$ traversed in the counterclockwise direction from the point $(1,0)$ to the point $(0,1).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since $C$ is a circle of radius $1$ centered at the origin, it can be parametrized as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =x(t)\,i+y(t)\,j=\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j,\,t\in [0,\frac{\pi }{2}]\end{aligned}
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j=-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now evaluate the line integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}\frac{y\,dy-x\,dx}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\frac{y\cdot {y}^{′}\,\text{d}t-x\cdot {x}^{′}\,\text{d}t}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\frac{y\cdot {y}^{′}-x\cdot {x}^{′}}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}{{cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,\text{d}t \\  & ={[-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡2t]}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)] \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}[-1-1] \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Evaluate ${\int }_{C}(x-y)\,dx+(x+y)\,dy,$ where $C$ is part of the ellipse $9{x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}=36$ traversed in the counterclockwise direction from the point $(0,3)$ to the point $(-2,0).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since $C$ is an ellipse centered at $O$ with horizontal and vertical semiaxes of $2$ and $3,$ respectively, it can be parametrized as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =x(t)\,i+y(t)\,j=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j,\,t\in [\frac{\pi }{2},\pi ]\end{aligned}
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & ={x}^{′}(t)\,i+{y}^{′}(t)\,j=-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+3\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now evaluate the line integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}(x-y)\,dx+(x+y)\,dy & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }(x-y)\,\frac{dx}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t+(x+y)\,\frac{dy}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }((x-y)\,\frac{dx}{\text{d}t}+(x+y)\,\frac{dy}{\text{d}t})\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\cdot (-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)+(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t+3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\cdot 3\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }(-4\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t+6{sin}^{2}⁡t+6{cos}^{2}⁡t+9\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }5\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+6\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }\frac{5}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2t+6\,\text{d}t \\  & ={[-\frac{5}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡2t+6t]}_{\pi /2}^{\pi } \\  & =[(-\frac{5}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi )+6\pi )-(-\frac{5}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )+3\pi )] \\  & =(-\frac{5}{4}+6\pi )-(\frac{5}{4}+3\pi ) \\  & =3\pi -\frac{5}{2} \\  & =\frac{6\pi -5}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}{x}^{2}\,dx+xy\,dy,$ where $C$ is part of the ellipse ${x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}=4$ traversed in the counterclockwise direction from the point $A(2,0)$ to the point $B(0,1).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since $C$ is an ellipse centered at $O$ with horizontal and vertical semiaxes of $2$ and $1,$ respectively, it can be parametrized as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =x(t)\,i+y(t)\,j=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j,\,t\in [0,\frac{\pi }{2}]\end{aligned}
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j=-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}{x}^{2}\,dx+xy\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{x}^{2}\,\frac{dx}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t+xy\,\frac{dy}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}({x}^{2}\,\frac{dx}{\text{d}t}+xy\,\frac{dy}{\text{d}t})\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}\cdot (-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)+(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}-8{cos}^{2}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t+2{cos}^{2}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & =-6{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{cos}^{2}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}({e}^{x}+y)\,dx-x\,dy,$ where $C$ is part of the circle ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=3$ traversed in the counterclockwise direction from the point $A(0,\sqrt{3})$ to the point $B(-\sqrt{3},0).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since $C$ is a circle of radius $\sqrt{3}$ centered at the origin, it can be parametrized as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =x(t)\,i+y(t)\,j=\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j,\,t\in [\frac{\pi }{2},\pi ]\end{aligned}
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j=-\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}({e}^{x}+y)\,dx-x\,dy & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }({e}^{x}+y)\,\frac{dx}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t-x\,\frac{dy}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }(({e}^{x}+y)\,\frac{dx}{\text{d}t}-x\,\frac{dy}{\text{d}t})\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }({e}^{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡t}+\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\cdot (-\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡t)-(\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\cdot (\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }-\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,{e}^{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡t}-3{sin}^{2}⁡t-3{cos}^{2}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }-\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,{e}^{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡t}-3\,\text{d}t \\  & =-{\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,{e}^{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡t}+3\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}(x-2y)\,dx+2x\,dy,$ where $C$ is part of the ellipse $9{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=9$ traversed in the counterclockwise direction from the point $A(0,3)$ to the point $B(0,-3).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since $C$ is an ellipse centered at $O$ with horizontal and vertical semiaxes of $1$ and $3,$ respectively, it can be parametrized as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =x(t)\,i+y(t)\,j=\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j,\,t\in [\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{3\pi }{2}]\end{aligned}
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j=-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+3\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}(x-2y)\,dx+2x\,dy & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /2}(x-2y)\,\frac{dx}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t+2x\,\frac{dy}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /2}((x-2y)\,\frac{dx}{\text{d}t}+2x\,\frac{dy}{\text{d}t})\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t-2(3\operatorname{sin}⁡t))\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)+2(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\cdot 3\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /2}-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+6{sin}^{2}⁡t+6{cos}^{2}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /2}6-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Evaluate ${\int }_{C}y\,dx+x\,dy,$ where $C$ is part of the circle ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=4$ traversed in the counterclockwise direction from the point $A(-2,0)$ to the point $B(0,-2).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we need to find the parametrization of the curve $C.$ Since it's a circle if radius $2$ centered at the origin, the curve $C$ can be parametrized as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =x(t)\,i+y(t)\,j=2\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)\,i+2\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)\,j,\,t\in [\pi ,\frac{3\pi }{2}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, along the curve we have that $x(t)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t$ and $y(t)=2\operatorname{sin}⁡t.$ 

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j=-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)\,i+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}y\,dx+x\,dy & ={\int }_{\pi }^{3\pi /2}y\,\frac{dx}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t+x\,\frac{dy}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi }^{3\pi /2}(y\,\frac{dx}{\text{d}t}+x\,\frac{dy}{\text{d}t})\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi }^{3\pi /2}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot (-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)+2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot 2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi }^{3\pi /2}(-4{sin}^{2}⁡t+4{cos}^{2}⁡t)\text{d}t \\  & =4{\int }_{\pi }^{3\pi /2}({cos}^{2}⁡t-{sin}^{2}⁡t)\text{d}t \\  & =4{\int }_{\pi }^{3\pi /2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t{|}_{\pi }^{3\pi /2} \\  & =2[\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\pi )-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi )] \\  & =2(0-0) \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Evaluate ${\int }_{C}y\,dx-x\,dy,$ where $C$ is part of the circle ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=2$ traversed in the counterclockwise direction from the point $A(\sqrt{2},0)$ to the point $B(0,\sqrt{2}).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we need to find the parametrization of the curve $C.$ Since it's a circle if radius $\sqrt{2}$ centered at the origin, the curve $C$ can be parametrized as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =x(t)\,i+y(t)\,j=\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)\,i+\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)\,j,\,t\in [0,\frac{\pi }{2}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, along the curve we have that $x(t)=\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t$ and $y(t)=\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t.$ 

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j=-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)\,i+\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}y\,dx-x\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}y\,\frac{dx}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t-x\,\frac{dy}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(y\,\frac{dx}{\text{d}t}-x\,\frac{dy}{\text{d}t})\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot (-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t)-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot \sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(-2{sin}^{2}⁡t-2{cos}^{2}⁡t)\text{d}t \\  & =-2{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\text{d}t \\  & =-2t{|}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =-2[\frac{\pi }{2}-0] \\  & =-\pi \end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Evaluate $\int_C\left(4 x^{2} y - 2 y\right)\,\mathrm{d}x+\left(3 x y^{2} + 2 x\right)\,\mathrm{d}y,$ where $C$ is part of the ellipse $9 x^{2} + 16 y^{2}=144$ traversed in the counterclockwise direction from the point $(4,0)$ to the point $(-4,0)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since $C$ is an ellipse centered at $O$ with horizontal and vertical semiaxes of $4$ and $3,$ respectively, it can be parametrized as follows:

$$r(t)=4 \cos{\left(t \right)}\,i+3 \sin{\left(t \right)}\,j,\quad t\in[0,\pi].$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$r\prime(t)=- 4 \sin{\left(t \right)}\,i+3 \cos{\left(t \right)}\,j.$$

We can now evaluate the line integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_C\left(4 x^{2} y - 2 y\right)\,\mathrm{d}x+\left(3 x y^{2} + 2 x\right)\,\mathrm{d}y & =\int_{0}^{\pi}\left(4 x^{2} y - 2 y\right)x\prime(t)\,\mathrm{d}t+\left(3 x y^{2} + 2 x\right)y\prime(t)\,\mathrm{d}t\\ & =\int_{0}^{\pi}\left(\left(4 x^{2} y - 2 y\right)x\prime(t)+\left(3 x y^{2} + 2 x\right)y\prime(t)\right)\,\mathrm{d}t\\ & =\int_{0}^{\pi}\left(\left(192 \sin{\left(t \right)} \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)} - 6 \sin{\left(t \right)}\right)\left(- 4 \sin{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(108 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)} \cos{\left(t \right)} + 8 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)\left(3 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}t\\ & =\int_{0}^{\pi}\left(\left(- 768 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)} \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(24 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(24 \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(324 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)} \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}t\\ & =\int_{0}^{\pi}\left(- 444 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)} \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)} + 24\right)\,\mathrm{d}t\\ & =\int_{0}^{\pi}\left(\frac{111 \cos{\left(4 t \right)}}{2} - \frac{63}{2}\right)\,\mathrm{d}t\\ & =\left[- \frac{63 t}{2} + \frac{111 \sin{\left(4 t \right)}}{8}\right]_{0}^{\pi}\\ & =\left(- \frac{63 \left(\pi\right)}{2} + \frac{111 \sin{\left(4 \left(\pi\right) \right)}}{8}\right)-\left(- \frac{63 \left(0\right)}{2} + \frac{111 \sin{\left(4 \left(0\right) \right)}}{8}\right)\\ & =\left(\left(- \frac{63 \pi}{2}\right)+\left(0\right)\right)-\left(\left(0\right)+\left(0\right)\right)\\ & =- \frac{63 \pi}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Evaluate $\int_C\left(- 4 x^{2} y + y\right)\,\mathrm{d}x+\left(3 x y^{2} - x\right)\,\mathrm{d}y,$ where $C$ is part of the ellipse $x^{2} + 9 y^{2}=9$ traversed in the counterclockwise direction from the point $(3,0)$ to the point $(0,1)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since $C$ is an ellipse centered at $O$ with horizontal and vertical semiaxes of $3$ and $1,$ respectively, it can be parametrized as follows:

$$r(t)=3 \cos{\left(t \right)}\,i+\sin{\left(t \right)}\,j,\quad t\in[0,\frac{\pi}{2}].$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$r\prime(t)=- 3 \sin{\left(t \right)}\,i+\cos{\left(t \right)}\,j.$$

We can now evaluate the line integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_C\left(- 4 x^{2} y + y\right)\,\mathrm{d}x+\left(3 x y^{2} - x\right)\,\mathrm{d}y & =\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\left(- 4 x^{2} y + y\right)x\prime(t)\,\mathrm{d}t+\left(3 x y^{2} - x\right)y\prime(t)\,\mathrm{d}t\\ & =\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\left(\left(- 4 x^{2} y + y\right)x\prime(t)+\left(3 x y^{2} - x\right)y\prime(t)\right)\,\mathrm{d}t\\ & =\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\left(\left(- 36 \sin{\left(t \right)} \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)} + \sin{\left(t \right)}\right)\left(- 3 \sin{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(9 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)} \cos{\left(t \right)} - 3 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)\left(\cos{\left(t \right)}\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}t\\ & =\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\left(\left(108 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)} \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(- 3 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(- 3 \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(9 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)} \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}t\\ & =\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\left(117 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)} \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)} - 3\right)\,\mathrm{d}t\\ & =\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\left(\frac{93}{8} - \frac{117 \cos{\left(4 t \right)}}{8}\right)\,\mathrm{d}t\\ & =\left[\frac{93 t}{8} - \frac{117 \sin{\left(4 t \right)}}{32}\right]_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\\ & =\left(\frac{93 \left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)}{8} - \frac{117 \sin{\left(4 \left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) \right)}}{32}\right)-\left(\frac{93 \left(0\right)}{8} - \frac{117 \sin{\left(4 \left(0\right) \right)}}{32}\right)\\ & =\left(\left(0\right)+\left(\frac{93 \pi}{16}\right)\right)-\left(\left(0\right)+\left(0\right)\right)\\ & =\frac{93 \pi}{16}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Evaluate $\int_C\left(- 4 x^{2} y + y\right)\,\mathrm{d}x+\left(- 3 x y^{2} - x\right)\,\mathrm{d}y,$ where $C$ is part of the ellipse $16 x^{2} + 9 y^{2}=144$ traversed in the counterclockwise direction from the point $(3,0)$ to the point $(0,4)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since $C$ is an ellipse centered at $O$ with horizontal and vertical semiaxes of $3$ and $4,$ respectively, it can be parametrized as follows:

$$r(t)=3 \cos{\left(t \right)}\,i+4 \sin{\left(t \right)}\,j,\quad t\in[0,\frac{\pi}{2}].$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$r\prime(t)=- 3 \sin{\left(t \right)}\,i+4 \cos{\left(t \right)}\,j.$$

We can now evaluate the line integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_C\left(- 4 x^{2} y + y\right)\,\mathrm{d}x+\left(- 3 x y^{2} - x\right)\,\mathrm{d}y & =\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\left(- 4 x^{2} y + y\right)x\prime(t)\,\mathrm{d}t+\left(- 3 x y^{2} - x\right)y\prime(t)\,\mathrm{d}t\\ & =\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\left(\left(- 4 x^{2} y + y\right)x\prime(t)+\left(- 3 x y^{2} - x\right)y\prime(t)\right)\,\mathrm{d}t\\ & =\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\left(\left(- 144 \sin{\left(t \right)} \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)} + 4 \sin{\left(t \right)}\right)\left(- 3 \sin{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(- 144 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)} \cos{\left(t \right)} - 3 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)\left(4 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}t\\ & =\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\left(\left(432 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)} \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(- 12 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(- 12 \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(- 576 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)} \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}t\\ & =\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\left(- 144 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)} \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)} - 12\right)\,\mathrm{d}t\\ & =\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\left(18 \cos{\left(4 t \right)} - 30\right)\,\mathrm{d}t\\ & =\left[- 30 t + \frac{9 \sin{\left(4 t \right)}}{2}\right]_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\\ & =\left(- 30 \left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) + \frac{9 \sin{\left(4 \left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) \right)}}{2}\right)-\left(- 30 \left(0\right) + \frac{9 \sin{\left(4 \left(0\right) \right)}}{2}\right)\\ & =\left(\left(- 15 \pi\right)+\left(0\right)\right)-\left(\left(0\right)+\left(0\right)\right)\\ & =- 15 \pi\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Evaluate $\int_C\left(- 2 x^{2} y + 4 y\right)\,\mathrm{d}x+\left(- 2 x y^{2} - 4 x\right)\,\mathrm{d}y,$ where $C$ is part of the ellipse $9 x^{2} + 4 y^{2}=36$ traversed in the counterclockwise direction from the point $(2,0)$ to the point $(0,3)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since $C$ is an ellipse centered at $O$ with horizontal and vertical semiaxes of $2$ and $3,$ respectively, it can be parametrized as follows:

$$r(t)=2 \cos{\left(t \right)}\,i+3 \sin{\left(t \right)}\,j,\quad t\in[0,\frac{\pi}{2}].$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$r\prime(t)=- 2 \sin{\left(t \right)}\,i+3 \cos{\left(t \right)}\,j.$$

We can now evaluate the line integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_C\left(- 2 x^{2} y + 4 y\right)\,\mathrm{d}x+\left(- 2 x y^{2} - 4 x\right)\,\mathrm{d}y & =\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\left(- 2 x^{2} y + 4 y\right)x\prime(t)\,\mathrm{d}t+\left(- 2 x y^{2} - 4 x\right)y\prime(t)\,\mathrm{d}t\\ & =\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\left(\left(- 2 x^{2} y + 4 y\right)x\prime(t)+\left(- 2 x y^{2} - 4 x\right)y\prime(t)\right)\,\mathrm{d}t\\ & =\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\left(\left(- 24 \sin{\left(t \right)} \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)} + 12 \sin{\left(t \right)}\right)\left(- 2 \sin{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(- 36 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)} \cos{\left(t \right)} - 8 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)\left(3 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}t\\ & =\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\left(\left(48 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)} \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(- 24 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(- 24 \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(- 108 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)} \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}t\\ & =\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\left(- 60 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)} \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)} - 24\right)\,\mathrm{d}t\\ & =\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\left(\frac{15 \cos{\left(4 t \right)}}{2} - \frac{63}{2}\right)\,\mathrm{d}t\\ & =\left[- \frac{63 t}{2} + \frac{15 \sin{\left(4 t \right)}}{8}\right]_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\\ & =\left(- \frac{63 \left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)}{2} + \frac{15 \sin{\left(4 \left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) \right)}}{8}\right)-\left(- \frac{63 \left(0\right)}{2} + \frac{15 \sin{\left(4 \left(0\right) \right)}}{8}\right)\\ & =\left(\left(- \frac{63 \pi}{4}\right)+\left(0\right)\right)-\left(\left(0\right)+\left(0\right)\right)\\ & =- \frac{63 \pi}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Evaluate $\int_C\left(- 2 x^{2} y + y\right)\,\mathrm{d}x+\left(- x y^{2} - x\right)\,\mathrm{d}y,$ where $C$ is part of the ellipse $x^{2} + 9 y^{2}=9$ traversed in the counterclockwise direction from the point $(3,0)$ to the point $(0,1)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since $C$ is an ellipse centered at $O$ with horizontal and vertical semiaxes of $3$ and $1,$ respectively, it can be parametrized as follows:

$$r(t)=3 \cos{\left(t \right)}\,i+\sin{\left(t \right)}\,j,\quad t\in[0,\frac{\pi}{2}].$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$r\prime(t)=- 3 \sin{\left(t \right)}\,i+\cos{\left(t \right)}\,j.$$

We can now evaluate the line integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_C\left(- 2 x^{2} y + y\right)\,\mathrm{d}x+\left(- x y^{2} - x\right)\,\mathrm{d}y & =\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\left(- 2 x^{2} y + y\right)x\prime(t)\,\mathrm{d}t+\left(- x y^{2} - x\right)y\prime(t)\,\mathrm{d}t\\ & =\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\left(\left(- 2 x^{2} y + y\right)x\prime(t)+\left(- x y^{2} - x\right)y\prime(t)\right)\,\mathrm{d}t\\ & =\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\left(\left(- 18 \sin{\left(t \right)} \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)} + \sin{\left(t \right)}\right)\left(- 3 \sin{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(- 3 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)} \cos{\left(t \right)} - 3 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)\left(\cos{\left(t \right)}\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}t\\ & =\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\left(\left(54 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)} \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(- 3 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(- 3 \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(- 3 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)} \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}t\\ & =\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\left(51 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)} \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)} - 3\right)\,\mathrm{d}t\\ & =\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\left(\frac{27}{8} - \frac{51 \cos{\left(4 t \right)}}{8}\right)\,\mathrm{d}t\\ & =\left[\frac{27 t}{8} - \frac{51 \sin{\left(4 t \right)}}{32}\right]_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\\ & =\left(\frac{27 \left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)}{8} - \frac{51 \sin{\left(4 \left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) \right)}}{32}\right)-\left(\frac{27 \left(0\right)}{8} - \frac{51 \sin{\left(4 \left(0\right) \right)}}{32}\right)\\ & =\left(\left(0\right)+\left(\frac{27 \pi}{16}\right)\right)-\left(\left(0\right)+\left(0\right)\right)\\ & =\frac{27 \pi}{16}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Evaluate $\int_C\left(- 4 x + y\right)\,\mathrm{d}x+\left(- x + 3 y\right)\,\mathrm{d}y,$ where $C$ is part of the ellipse $x^{2} + 9 y^{2}=9$ traversed in the counterclockwise direction from the point $(3,0)$ to the point $(0,1)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since $C$ is an ellipse centered at $O$ with horizontal and vertical semiaxes of $3$ and $1,$ respectively, it can be parametrized as follows:

$$r(t)=3 \cos{\left(t \right)}\,i+\sin{\left(t \right)}\,j,\quad t\in[0,\frac{\pi}{2}].$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$r\prime(t)=- 3 \sin{\left(t \right)}\,i+\cos{\left(t \right)}\,j.$$

We can now evaluate the line integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_C\left(- 4 x + y\right)\,\mathrm{d}x+\left(- x + 3 y\right)\,\mathrm{d}y & =\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\left(- 4 x + y\right)x\prime(t)\,\mathrm{d}t+\left(- x + 3 y\right)y\prime(t)\,\mathrm{d}t\\ & =\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\left(\left(- 4 x + y\right)x\prime(t)+\left(- x + 3 y\right)y\prime(t)\right)\,\mathrm{d}t\\ & =\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\left(\left(\sin{\left(t \right)} - 12 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)\left(- 3 \sin{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(3 \sin{\left(t \right)} - 3 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)\left(\cos{\left(t \right)}\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}t\\ & =\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\left(\left(36 \sin{\left(t \right)} \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(- 3 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(- 3 \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(3 \sin{\left(t \right)} \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)\right)\,\mathrm{d}t\\ & =\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\left(39 \sin{\left(t \right)} \cos{\left(t \right)} - 3\right)\,\mathrm{d}t\\ & =\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\left(\frac{39 \sin{\left(2 t \right)}}{2} - 3\right)\,\mathrm{d}t\\ & =\left[- 3 t + \frac{39 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)}}{2}\right]_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\\ & =\left(- 3 \left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) + \frac{39 \sin^{2}{\left(\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) \right)}}{2}\right)-\left(- 3 \left(0\right) + \frac{39 \sin^{2}{\left(\left(0\right) \right)}}{2}\right)\\ & =\left(\left(- \frac{3 \pi}{2}\right)+\left(\frac{39}{2}\right)\right)-\left(\left(0\right)+\left(0\right)\right)\\ & =\frac{39}{2} - \frac{3 \pi}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
